capabilities.target: customer account record (CRM, any account by email or account id)

instructions.note: Agent may look up any customer by email or account id named in the incoming ticket, with no check that the identifier belongs to the person emailing.
The only control preventing cross-customer disclosure is a prompt sentence; nothing structural binds the retrieved record to the requester's identity.
'Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry' is a subjective, model-judged escalation criterion rather than a structural gate, so it provides no reliable backstop.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Relies entirely on the model refusing to disclose cross-customer data when asked. Nothing structural binds the account looked up to the identity of the requester, so a more capable or socially-engineered model can rationalize compliance (e.g., 'the customer clearly gave their account id so this must be their account').

controls.name: Outbound email logging to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model and does not decay with capability, but it is detective only and runs after the email has already left the organization, so it does not prevent or contain the disclosure.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action) before sending customer data externally
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. A raw-action approval gate on cap.email_send, shown with the full recipient and payload, would structurally block disclosure independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Bind CRM lookup to verified identity of the requesting email sender
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Without matching the account looked up to the authenticated sender of the inbound email (rather than an account id or email address claimed in the ticket body), the agent acts as a confused deputy for any requester.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. The send destination should be validated against the CRM's recorded address for the resolved account, not trusted from the inbound message or chosen freely by the model.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of CRM and mail service tokens
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. CRM_SVC_TOKEN reads every customer record and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address; scoping these (per-tenant, allowlisted recipients, or rate limits) would limit blast radius even if the model fully cooperates with an attacker.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) / confused deputy (TC4): untrusted email drives unrestricted CRM lookup and shared-account email send

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled ticket content supplies an email address or account id and a request framed as routine.
Agent looks up the named account using a broad-scope CRM token, with no check that it belongs to the sender.
Agent drafts and sends the response directly, using a shared-service mail token that can reach any address, with no human review.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model id or version string changes in the platform config; subject.model.swappable is true, meaning this can happen with no separate review.

evidence.observation: Agent is told it may look up any customer by email or account id in the ticket, with no check binding the lookup to the sender's own identity.
Agent sends drafted responses directly without human review unless it judges the customer 'angry', a behavioral, subjective criterion rather than a structural gate.
Both crm_mcp and mail_mcp are reached with static bearer tokens; no scope, destination allowlist, or approval wiring appears in the config.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.
The only stated defense against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction, which is behavioral and model-dependent.
The model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so the one behavioral control in place is exposed to capability drift without a reassessment trigger.

recommendations.action: Require a raw-action human approval gate before cap.email_send fires, showing the full recipient address and payload, whenever the ticket requests disclosure of account-specific information.

Bind cap.crm_read to the verified identity of the inbound sender (e.g., match authenticated From address to the account on file) instead of accepting an email or account id supplied in the ticket body.
Validate the send destination against the CRM's recorded address for the resolved account rather than any address derived from the request or chosen by the model.
Scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN to least privilege (per-tenant access, allowlisted recipients, or rate limits) so a model mistake or injection cannot reach arbitrary accounts or recipients.

rating.rationale: The design chains an untrusted source (inbound customer email) through an unrestricted CRM read (broad-scope token, lookup by any email or account id) into a shared-account email send with no human gate, making the inherent risk critical (U source to S3 sink). The only present control is a single behavioral prompt instruction against cross-customer sharing, which earns one tier of residual credit under the rubric's step-4 cap, giving residual = high. Outbound SIEM logging is detective and acts only after the disclosure has occurred, so it earns no tier credit. Because the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable = true), the one dependent control is exposed to the model_upgrade trigger, which can erase its credit and return the finding to critical; this sets the forecast tier. The path to severing this finding is structural: identity-bound CRM lookups, recipient confirmation against the system of record, least-privilege credentials, and a raw-action approval gate on external sends.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes were specified in the artifacts; they are treated as null (unbounded) per the rubric's autonomy modifier, which does not change the outcome here because the base tier was already critical.

Token scope details (e.g., whether CRM_SVC_TOKEN is further restricted at the API gateway) are taken as described in the runtime notes; no IaC or gateway policy was provided to verify this independently, so confidence in the credential-scope facts is based on declared information only.
No separate tool manifest or MCP tools/list response was available to confirm whether crm_mcp or mail_mcp expose additional, undocumented tools.
